outcome: Areal bone mineral density (aBMD) of the lumbar spine
Areal bone mineral density (aBMD) of the femoral neck
cohort: The study included 1217 postmenopausal women aged 69.2 +/- 6.4 years from the Bushehr Elderly Health (BEH) program.
finding: Grand multiparity is associated with significantly lower areal bone mineral density of the lumbar spine and femoral neck, and a lower trabecular bone score, indicating deleterious effects on bone health.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken at the time of recruitment, when participants were postmenopausal, with an average age of 69.2 years.
